key_insight: Fixed, hand-crafted schema graphs are not required for effective relational deep learning — learning full-resolution graph structure end-to-end from the data preserves relational semantics while yielding better adaptability and performance.
problem_solved: Removes reliance on brittle, manually designed schema graphs for relational databases by enabling automatic discovery of high-fidelity graph structure that retains full-resolution entities and relations.
method: Represent the relational database at full resolution (individual tuples/attributes as graph nodes) rather than compressing by schema-level shortcuts.
Learn the graph adjacency/edge weights jointly with a GNN in an end-to-end differentiable manner, using sparsity and relational consistency regularizers to keep semantics.
Train the structure learner and GNN together for downstream relational prediction tasks, enabling the model to adapt structure to data noise and task signal.
impact: Makes relational deep learning more robust, less manual, and better suited to real-world, messy RDBs — reducing engineering effort and improving generalization across schemas and datasets.
visual_elements: Before/after diagram: hand-crafted schema graph vs. learned full-resolution graph (nodes = tuples/attributes).
Pipeline flowchart: RDB → full-resolution graph construction → differentiable structure learner + GNN → prediction.
Bar chart or table: performance comparison (fixed-schema methods vs. learned-structure) on key relational tasks.
Adjacency heatmap or edge-weight visualization showing how the learned structure differs from the original schema.
paper_title: Is Fixing Schema Graphs Necessary? Full-Resolution Graph Structure Learning for Relational Deep Learning
paper_authors: Yi Huang, Qingyun Sun, Jia Li, Xingcheng Fu, Jianxin Li
